messages:
edr-bot: ALERT — High severity EDR detection on host ALC-WS-09 (alice.chen). Detection: Win.Mal.Exfil. Quarantined file: C:\Users\alice.chen\AppData\Roaming\tmp\updater.exe. SHA256: d1f8e2a9b3c4f5e6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0. No immediate network connections noted in agent telemetry.
security-oncall: I'm taking this. @alice.chen — are you at your desk? Any popups, unexpected prompts, or USBs attached? Please keep laptop online and do not reboot until we say so. :eyes:
alice.chen: saw a strange "Updater" popup earlier, machine felt sluggish. No USBs. I can keep it online and not close lid.
rajiv_k: any signs of data exfil? last active outbound IPs?
luke_ops: Can you run these in an elevated PowerShell and paste outputs? If you're not comfortable, we can remote into EDR live session.
```
Get-FileHash -Path "C:\Users\alice.chen\AppData\Roaming\tmp\updater.exe" -Algorithm SHA256
Get-MpThreat -Verbose
netstat -ano | findstr /i "established" # check for active connections
Get-Process -Id (Get-Process -Name updater -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```
marta-garcia: I've kicked off a full EDR scan and uploaded the quarantined sample to our sandbox (ticket SND-4231). Initial sandbox verdict: suspicious behavior — attempts to enumerate credential stores and list mounted drives. No confirmed exfil traffic in sandbox.
it-support: EDR live session attached. File was quarantined at 2024-04-03T14:10:22Z by agent v5.2.1. Agent logs show the process spawned from %APPDATA% and had child process cmd.exe. No persistent service created (no registry run keys). Collecting full triage bundle now.
edr-bot: Agent telemetry snippet -> child process tree: updater.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe -EncodedCommand ... (truncated). Observed API calls to WinHTTP but no successful remote POSTs recorded.
security-oncall: Good work. @luke_ops please grab the EDR artifact and check for scheduled tasks, services, Run keys, WMI persistence, and recent RDP sessions. Also check for any recently created local accounts. @marta-garcia did you get the process memory dump uploaded?
marta-garcia: memory dump uploaded to secure share (forensics/samples/1711539802/). No scheduled tasks. Found one anomalous entry in TaskCache: LastWriteTime 2024-04-03T13:58Z — flagged for review.
alice.chen: attaching output of Get-FileHash and netstat below.
```
SHA256 (C:\Users\alice.chen\AppData\Roaming\tmp\updater.exe) = d1f8e2a9b3c4f5e6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0
(no established TCP connections)
```
luke_ops: No active established connections is good. I'll run persistence checks and IOC hunts across recent telemetry. Can you also confirm whether alice had any elevated token use to cloud services in the last 24h? Security team, check KMS/AWS CloudTrail for decrypt or GenerateDataKey calls from alice's principal.
security-oncall: On it — querying CloudTrail and KMS logs now for any unusual calls. If we see any KMS decrypts, we'll rotate affected CMKs and rotate user/service credentials.
it-support: For containment: laptop quarantined from corporate network (moved to isolated VLAN) and block applied to alice's SSO sessions. Manager informed. We'll collect a forensic image and arrange swap unit. Do we want to force password/MFA reset org-wide for alice's sessions?
rajiv_k: Recommend reset of alice's SSO session tokens and any short-lived API keys she used on her device. Also rotate any deploy keys she may have had local access to. We'll scope after we see CloudTrail.
security-oncall: Action items so far: 1) Forensic image and preserve EDR artifacts (it-support) 2) Re-image laptop and rebuild (it-support) 3) Rotate SSO session tokens + require MFA re-enroll (it-support) 4) Cloud audit: check KMS, CloudTrail for decrypt/GenerateDataKey in past 48h (security-oncall) 5) Org hunt for SHA256 and related IOCs (luke_ops & marta-garcia) 6) Postmortem & timeline (security-oncall). I'll open an incident tracker entry and assign owners. :white_check_mark:
marta-garcia: Sandbox behavior indicates credential access attempts. We've exported indicators: mutex names, file hashes, YARA hits. Running org-wide search via EDR queries for any matching indicators now.
edr-bot: EDR query result: no other endpoints matched SHA256 in last 30 days. One endpoint had a related binary with different hash but same compile timestamp — investigating.
luke_ops: Found one suspicious scheduled task timestamp in two endpoints; tasks not executed. Flagging them for removal and scheduling targeted scans. Escalating to on-call infra team to check lateral movement possibilities.
security-oncall: Please notify @people-ops and alice's manager that device is off-network and being rebuilt. We're not declaring a data breach at this time — no confirmed exfil. Keep communications minimal and factual.
it-support: User provided laptop to IT at 16:30 local. Forensic image taken, then reimage scheduled. We will preserve disk image and upload to case folder.
alice.chen: thanks team. appreciate quick response.
security-oncall: Post-incident follow-ups planned: 1) Rotate any keys/tokens accessed from device (incl. ephemeral keys) 2) Review RBAC for local admin privileges on endpoints — consider tightening policy 3) Add SHA256/IOCs to permanent detection rules 4) Run targeted KMS access audit and rotate if any suspicious decrypts found 5) Update onboarding docs to remind users not to install unsigned updaters. We'll draft a short postmortem and share with execs once triage complete. :memo:
marta-garcia: tagging for follow-up: evidence retention path, sandbox report, and hunts all in incident folder. ETA for initial postmortem draft: 24-48h.
security-oncall: Closing active containment here. If anyone finds new matches, reactivate and ping #incidents. Thanks everyone. :tada:
